summary: The returned abstracts do not establish internal cavities in RNA condensates. S1 directly reports two-RNA/PEG condensates in which purine-rich RNAs act as phase-separating scaffolds and pyrimidine-rich RNAs with weaker heterotypic interactions adsorb to and wet interfaces of coexisting scaffold phases; simulations and tracking address interfacial orientation/dynamics. This supports an interface-localization relation under those conditions, not cavity formation or a mapping from alpha to f. S5 reports a protein client (SMN) modulating GAR1-RNA condensate architecture through competitive RNA interactions, but this is a protein-RNA system and abstract-only. S2-S4 are broad perspectives/reviews. Therefore H1 remains speculative, refined to an interface-wetting bridge with explicit transfer conditions. C2L1-alpha remains conditional endpoint arithmetic, not a composition series.

hypotheses.status: new, explicitly speculative bridge hypothesis refined using abstract-level relation
hypotheses.statement: Conditional bridge: if one transcribed RNA species in the case behaves as a scaffold and another as a weaker-binding adsorbent, composition-dependent adsorption/wetting at internal interfaces could stabilize RNA-poor domains inside the scaffold-rich network. This extends S1's reported wetting of coexisting phase interfaces to internal domains in a transcribing four-arm RNA condensate; neither the species roles nor internal cavity formation is established here. At fixed reaction chemistry, measured RNA loading should alter interface enrichment and cavity incidence/area if this bridge holds.

The phase endpoints are not comparable to the imaging reaction or do not represent its mixture range; cavities arise from amplification carryover or another reaction-state change independently of composition-driven internal domains. Constant selectivity under matched conditions remains possible.

equations: A possible interfacial bridge would require Gamma_i = integral_over_interface (c_i(local)-c_i(bulk reference)) dz; no profiles, interfacial thickness, or surface excess are provided, so this is a measurement definition, not an evaluated law.
At dense-phase volume fraction phi, dense-phase variant mass fraction=phi*Cv_dense/[phi*Cv_dense+(1-phi)*Cv_dilute]; it is not f and requires phase volumes.
